Events.RelatedBody: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The Blazor WebAssembly development-server debug page can reflect unencoded exception text, allowing cross-origin script injection through the unauthenticated `/_framework/debug` endpoint used by `dotnet watch`. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69802 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-79 (Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.12 | 10.0.13 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.31 | 8.0.32 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.20 | 9.0.21 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.32 Runtime or .NET 8.0.426 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.21 Runtime or .NET 9.0.319 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.13 Runtime or .NET 10.0.402 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. * If you're using .NET 11.0, you should download and install .NET 11.0.0-rc.2 Runtime or .NET 11.0.100-rc.2 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/11.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-96230](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-96230) ### Acknowledgements - Kevin Gosse ### Revisions V1.0 (10/13/2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Assembly version for DispatchProxy shim is too low resulting in duplicate types for DispatchProxy
Issues.Body:
Create a new `netstandard2.1` library.
Add a reference to `<PackageReference Include="System.Reflection.DispatchProxy" Version="4.7.1" />`
Try to use `DispatchProxy`

Expected: 
`DispatchProxy` is resolved from `netstandard.dll`

Actual:
```
error CS0433: The type 'DispatchProxy' exists in both 'System.Reflection.DispatchProxy, Version=4.0.6.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a' and 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51'
```


Build contains conflict message:
```
Encountered conflict between 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' and 'Runtime:C:\Program Files\dotnet\packs\NETStandard.Library.Ref\2.1.0\ref\netstandard2.1\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll'. Choosing 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' because AssemblyVersion '4.0.6.0' is greater than '4.0.5.0'.
```

Other shims avoid this by setting the AssemblyVersion higher than that which was previously shipped.

Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs " (#1775)

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: [BUG] [UWP] GetManifestResourceInfo doesn't work on UWP
Issues.Body:
# Summary
I was trying to access Embedded resources on UWP. Something like this

```C#
manifestResourceInfo = typeof(App).Assembly.GetManifestResourceInfo("UwpEmbeddedResourceBug.appsettings.json");
```
However, this doesn't work on UWP, even though it works like a charm on iOS for instance. 
Further, when you try to use this in UWP debug mode, it will return non-null `manifestResourceInfo`, however internally the `FileName` property will be null. But if you try to use the same on Release build, instead you will get an exception

```
System.PlatformNotSupportedException: Operation is not supported on this platform.
   at System.Func`1.BeginInvoke(AsyncCallback, Object) + 0x1f
   at SharedLibrary!<BaseAddress>+0x9f17d7
   at UwpEmbeddedResourceBug.MainPage..ctor() + 0x3e
```
## Sample project

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem" (#1792)

Issues.Title: Strong name signature not valid
Issues.Body:
Since I've ported a ClickOnce application from .NET Framework 4.6.1 to .NET Standard 2.0, the message _"Strong assembly name signature not valid for **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**"_ appears when trying to install or update the application. So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh
> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:
  - [Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects)
    - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment
      - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Authoring
        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**
- This issue appears on windows server machines but the software runs on different machines and I would like to avoid temporary workarounds such as editing the registry and activate the strong name bypass feature because of the forced validation on windows server machines
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Strong name signature not valid" (#1789)

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

We have directed your feedback to the appropriate engineering team for further evaluation. The team will review the feedback and notify you about the next steps.

#### Raphael Affolter on 2/7/2020, 08:39 AM:

Because we print a lot, we really suffer from this performance penalty.

Also reading PaperSizes and PaperSources from the printer settings is slow caused by the same problem.

Could you please inform me about a possible fix?

Best Regards,

Raphael

#### Raphael Affolter on 2/7/2020, 10:33 AM:

In my opinion the fix is easy: replace GetOutputPort by OutputPort in the call to

FastDeviceCapabilities.

Done.

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: Reduce symbol-search startup cost after interrupted updates
Issues.Body:
Closing Visual Studio while it is updating its package-search data can leave it rebuilding the same data on every later launch. This data helps Visual Studio suggest the NuGet package or reference assembly that provides a missing type.

This is being constantly hit in the performance lab.

Roslyn saves two copies: the downloaded text, and a binary file containing the already-built search index. Previously, it saved the text first. If Visual Studio closed before the binary copy was saved, the next launch had to parse the text and build the index again. Saving the missing binary copy also waited for an online update check, so short sessions or slow connections could keep repeating that work.

This change saves the ready-to-load binary copy first and can use it even if the text copy was not saved. It also repairs existing text-only copies without waiting for the server.

The improvement is avoiding repeated work, not making text parsing faster. A healthy binary copy already loads in about 8 ms in both versions, and the initial download and index build are still required.

An isolated test of loading this background data after an interrupted update measured:

| Work per launch | Previously | With this change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Time to load the data, median | 933 ms | 8.3 ms |
| Bytes allocated while loading, median | 165.1 MB | 25.1 MB |

These are background data-loading measurements, not Add New Item dialog timings or a measurement of overall Visual Studio startup.

<details>
<summary>Measurement setup and additional results</summary>

The test used the public NuGet index in a Release/x64 .NET Framework harness with simulated file I/O and download responses. Each version ran 8 repetitions of 5 launches, for 40 measured loads.

| Additional measurement | Previously | With this change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Load time, 95th percentile | 1028.6 ms | 9.47 ms |
| CPU time per load, average | 906.3 ms | 7.03 ms |
| Garbage collections across all 40 loads, Gen0 / Gen1 / Gen2 | 534 / 195 / 30 | 0 / 0 / 0 |

An existing text-only copy needs one conversion before later launches can use the binary copy. That first conversion allocated 236.1 MB in this test; subsequent loads allocated about 25.1 MB. Garbage-collection pause times were not collected.

</details>

 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/86132)

Issues.Title: roslyn-language-server: `--telemetryLevel off` still creates and starts the default telemetry session
Issues.Body:
### Version Used

`roslyn-language-server.osx-arm64` 5.13.0-1.26514.10 (dotnet/roslyn d82b7f7d). The same code is on `main` at e4e2833b. Every build from 5.12.0-1.26475.2 on behaves this way; 5.11.0 does not.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the server outside VS Code and C# Dev Kit, with telemetry off, and HOME set to an empty folder so you can see what it writes:
   ```sh
   HOME=/tmp/empty-home dotnet Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.LanguageServer.dll --stdio --logLevel Information --telemetryLevel off --extensionLogDirectory /tmp/logs
   ```
2. Before sending any message, look at what it has written and which hosts it has connected to.

We hit this in [Passenger](https://github.com/Zaneris/passenger), an open-source C# IDE that runs `roslyn-language-server` from NuGet, always with `--telemetryLevel off`.

### Expected Behavior

With `--telemetryLevel off`, no telemetry session is created. The server's README says "Pass `--telemetryLevel off` to disable telemetry" (#86066). 5.11.0 created no session without Dev Kit: `GetTelemetryLevel` returned a level only when `DevKitDependencyPath` or `COPILOT_TELEMETRY_LEVEL` was set.

### Actual Behavior

`Program.Main` calls `LanguageServerTelemetry.CreateSession(..., isDefaultSession: true)`. `CreateSession` returns null only when the level is null, or when it is `"off"` for a session that **isn't** the default one:

```csharp
if (serverConfiguration.TelemetryLevel is not { } telemetryLevel ||
    (!isDefaultSession && telemetryLevel == "off"))
{
    return null;
}
```

So with `off` the default session is still built. `InitializeSession` then does all of the following, with only `IsOptedIn` set to false:
- `TelemetryService.SetDefaultSession(session)`
- `session.Start()` and `session.RegisterForReliabilityEvent()`
- registers the event and metric sinks
- `FaultReporter.InitializeFatalErrorHandlers()`

What we see with `--telemetryLevel off` on macOS:
- **It loads `Microsoft.VisualStudio.RemoteControl`.** A copy of the server without that assembly ends at startup with `FileNotFoundException` before reading a message. 5.11.0 never loaded it.
- **It writes files under `$HOME/Library/Application Support` before any message is sent:**
  - `Microsoft/ApplicationInsights/vstelf3e86b4023cc43f0be495508d51f588a/`
  - `Microsoft/registry/CurrentUser/software/microsoft/visualstudio/telemetry/persistentpropertybag/microsoft.codeanalysis.languageserver/values.xml`
  - `Microsoft/DeveloperTools/deviceid`, `Microsoft/DeveloperTools/.hwcache/uuid`, `Microsoft/DeveloperTools/.hwcache/hardDriveSerialNumber`
  - `Microsoft DevDiv/Installation/InstallationId.txt`, `DevMachineId.txt`, `.hwcache/uuid.txt`, `.hwcache/driveserial.txt`
- **It opens an outgoing HTTPS connection before any message is sent.** The connection went to 24.226.33.17:443, an address `telemetry.visualstudio.microsoft.com` resolved to at the time, and stayed open for the 25 seconds we watched (`lsof -i` on the server's process).

For an editor whose users chose `off`, that means a session that computes and stores machine and disk identifiers, and makes outgoing connections, even though nothing is reported.

### Suggested fix

Return null for `"off"` for the default session too, as `CreateSession` already does for every other session:

```csharp
if (serverConfiguration.TelemetryLevel is not { } telemetryLevel || telemetryLevel == "off")
{
    return null;
}
```

Issues.Title: Support attributes on individual C# union cases
Issues.Body:
### Proposal

Allow attributes to be applied to individual case types in a union declaration:

```csharp
union Foo([MyAttribute] int, string);
```

The annotation would describe the `int` case within `Foo`, rather than the underlying `int` type or the union as a whole.

### Motivation

Serialization libraries need to associate metadata with individual union cases—for example, stable aliases or discriminator values that do not depend on declaration order or CLR type names.

A concrete example of this requirement is [AArnott/Nerdbank.MessagePack#1119](https://github.com/AArnott/Nerdbank.MessagePack/issues/1119), which requests configurable serialization aliases for C# union cases. Case annotations would provide a declarative way for libraries to support such customization. I also described the missing language support in [my response in eiriktsarpalis/PolyType#537](https://github.com/eiriktsarpalis/PolyType/issues/537#issuecomment-6261151248).

Annotating the underlying case type is not equivalent: it may be a built-in or third-party type, and the metadata may need to differ between unions containing the same type.

### Possible lowering

My expectation is that the attribute could be emitted on the synthesized constructor corresponding to the annotated case—`Foo(int)` in this example—making it discoverable through reflection and Roslyn’s symbol model.

However, I defer to the language/compiler maintainers on the most appropriate attribute target and lowering strategy. The core request is a way to associate user-defined attributes with a specific union case.

cc @AlekseyTs — following up on our offline discussion.

Issues.Title: Make anonymous delegate numbering deterministic
Issues.Body:
Fixes #86096

Generic anonymous delegates with optional or `params` parameters kept the source location of whichever use was compiled first, so thread scheduling could change their numbered names. Update the shared template to its earliest source location using the existing atomic `AdjustLocation` method, matching the other anonymous template paths. An inline comment explains why the update is needed.

The regression covers lambdas and method groups, optional and `params` parameters, and generic and pointer signatures. It checks source-order numbering and byte-for-byte identical assemblies with concurrent compilation enabled and disabled.

The new generic cases failed **deterministically** before the fix: nested partial classes force the serial compiler to visit later source uses first. Concurrent compilation can visit the types in a different order and pass before the fix; the regression does not depend on catching an intermittent race.

Additional script-submission cases cover delegate templates reused from an earlier compilation. Removing only the ownership check makes both cases fail deterministically during emission, because `AdjustLocation` attempts to compare source locations from different compilations.

Issues.Title: Fix Native AOT CLI localization
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes dotnet/sdk#55820.

Referenced satellites lacked the `AssetType=resources` metadata needed for inclusion in the native image, leaving CLI help unlocalized.

This builds on dotnet/sdk#55781, which already restores native UI language initialization and includes Configurer satellites.

### Changes

- Mark own and referenced satellite publish assets as resources.
- Generalize the bootstrap SDK's Configurer-only workaround to all published reference satellites, excluding compiler inputs already selected.
- Add localization regression coverage and contributor guidance.

### Validation

- Published and ran the **full Native AOT test executable on Windows x64: 233 passed, zero failed or skipped**, including the 13-culture help matrix and cached-run integration tests.
- Negative control: substituting the bootstrap native library made all three native translation checks fail while the three managed baseline checks still passed. Restoring the candidate returned the full suite to green.
- PowerShell/Bash runner syntax, documentation links, and whitespace checks passed.

Linux and macOS execution await the new CI run.

**Note:** dotnet/sdk#56378 changes the CLI to load localized resources directly from satellite assemblies instead of embedding them.

Issues.Title: Fix vulnerable MessagePack and ApiCompat cryptography dependencies
Issues.Body:
## Summary

The baseline audited solution restore reports NU1902/NU1903 for System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 8.0.1 in ApiCompat and NU1902 for MessagePack 3.1.8 in SDK test projects.

- Update the central MessagePack pin to 3.1.9.
- Explicitly reference Pkcs 8.0.2 in ApiCompat.Task and PackageValidation, which intentionally disable transitive pinning. Preserve NuGet's existing dependency major version, PackageValidation's runtime exclusion, and private ApiCompat tool deployment.
- Apply the task reference only to .NET targets. During source-build, omit the toolset version override so central source-built versions remain authoritative.
- Leave analyzer test dependencies unchanged: their restored graphs do not contain the crypto versions affected by these advisories.
- Do not change audit settings or re-enable broad transitive pinning.

Public advisories: [MessagePack](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qhrr-8q5h-9q3h), [Pkcs](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2fmv-rv2c-59x7), and [additional Pkcs advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-846f-f764-76mx).

Related servicing fixes: dotnet/sdk#56709 and dotnet/sdk#56710.

## Validation

- Reproduced the baseline warnings, then passed a full `sdk.slnx` restore with `NuGetAudit=true`, `NuGetAuditMode=all`, and NU1900-NU1905 promoted to errors. No audit suppressions added.
- Checked restored assets: no MessagePack 3.1.8 or Pkcs 8.0.1 remains; ApiCompat resolves Pkcs 8.0.2.
- Built ApiCompat.Task and its project dependencies successfully for net10.0 with zero warnings/errors.
- Evaluated both ApiCompat projects with `DotNetBuildSourceOnly=true`; neither retains the toolset version override.
- Product tests, a complete source-build, and the internal TestTemplatesCG job were not run. Public PR CI is not a substitute for that internal CG job.

> [!NOTE]
> AI-generated with GitHub Copilot.

# [release/11.0.1xx] Fix Hot Reload on static SSR pages in Blazor Web apps

Restore browser refresh for static SSR pages without starting WebAssembly.

## Description

Backports #56644 to `release/11.0.1xx`. Restores automatic browser refresh for static SSR pages in Blazor Web apps while preserving Hot Reload when navigating to interactive components.

Fixes #56428

## Customer Impact

`dotnet watch` reports applied changes, but static SSR pages in Blazor Web apps using WebAssembly or Auto interactivity do not refresh. Developers must refresh manually.

- [x] Yes
- [ ] No

Regressed between SDK `11.0.100-rc.2.26474.118` and `11.0.100-rc.2.26475.136`.

## Risk

- [ ] High
- [ ] Medium
- [x] Low

Limited to development-time Hot Reload JavaScript. Reuses the existing authenticated connection, client-owned keypair, and runtime apply APIs; published application behavior is unchanged.

## Verification

- [x] Manual (required)
- [x] Automated

## Packaging changes reviewed?

- [ ] Yes
- [ ] No
- [x] N/A

Issues.Title: Workload set 10.0.402.1 references unpublished microsoft.net.sdk.ios.manifest-10.0.100 27.1.10018; dotnet workload install fails
Issues.Body:
Since workload set 10.0.402.1 was published (2026-10-19, ~19:30 UTC), `dotnet workload install wasm-tools` fails on CI agents that take the latest workload set:

```
Checking for updated workload version.
Skipping NuGet package signature verification.
Installing workload version 10.0.402.1.
Installing workload manifest microsoft.net.workload.emscripten.current version 10.0.113...
...
Installing workload manifest microsoft.net.sdk.android version 36.1.118...
Installing workload manifest microsoft.net.sdk.ios version 27.1.10018...
Workload installation failed. Rolling back installed packs...
Installation rollback failed: Workload manifest microsoft.net.sdk.ios: 27.1.10018/10.0.100 from workload version 10.0.402.1 was not installed. Running "dotnet workload repair" may resolve this.
Workload installation failed: Failed to install manifest microsoft.net.sdk.ios version 27.1.10018: Version 27.1.10018 of package microsoft.net.sdk.ios.manifest-10.0.100 is not found in NuGet feeds https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json..
```

- The newest `microsoft.net.sdk.ios.manifest-10.0.100` on nuget.org is 27.0.10722; 27.1.10018 is not published.
- The bump appears to come from dotnet/workload-versions#996 ("[release/10] Update dependencies from dotnet/macios", merged 2026-10-19 18:16 UTC), shipped in `microsoft.net.workloads.10.0.400` 10.402.1.
- Installing a workload unrelated to iOS (`wasm-tools`) still fails, because every manifest of the workload set is installed.
- Workload set 10.0.402.0 installs fine.

Several projects are already pinning their workload set or SDK to work around it, for example AgOpenGPS-Official/AgOpenWeb#361, krovomi/Lettra#156, martin-stromberg/VideoPlayer-App#70 and zymasystems/Solvix-StockFlow#6.

**Expected:** a workload set is published only once every manifest it references is on nuget.org, or 10.0.402.1 is unlisted until the iOS manifest is published.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Workload set 10.0.402.1 references unpublished microsoft.net.sdk.ios.manifest-10.0.100 27.1.10018; dotnet workload install fails" (#56708)

Issues.Title: [release/10.0.4xx] Fix vulnerable MessagePack and cryptography dependency resolutions
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fix vulnerable dependency resolutions on `release/10.0.4xx` without changing the branch's NuGet audit policy or enabling transitive pinning in projects that deliberately disable it.

- Update the central MessagePack pin from 3.1.8 to 3.1.9.
- Update System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs and Xml from 10.0.12 to 10.0.13, together with System.Formats.Asn1 10.0.13 required by the patched Pkcs package. Update dependency provenance from the published NuGet package metadata and regenerate Version.Details.props using Darc's generator.
- Explicitly reference Pkcs 8.0.2 in ApiCompat.Task and PackageValidation, preserving their existing dependency major version, runtime asset exclusions, and private tool deployment behavior.
- Add explicit Pkcs and Xml references in NetAnalyzers unit tests so the patched central versions apply.
- Leave the ApiCompat toolset version override unset during source-build so central source-built package versions remain authoritative.

Public advisories: [MessagePack](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qhrr-8q5h-9q3h), [Pkcs](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2fmv-rv2c-59x7), [additional Pkcs advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-846f-f764-76mx), and [Xml](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r955-8q5j-3h83).

## Validation

- Full `sdk.slnx` restore passed with `NuGetAudit=true`, `NuGetAuditMode=all`, and no audit warning suppressions. Existing non-audit warning exclusions were retained.
- Inspected restored assets: MessagePack 3.1.9; ApiCompat Pkcs 8.0.2; central Pkcs, Xml, and Asn1 10.0.13.
- ApiCompat.Task and its project dependencies built for net8.0 and net472 with no warnings or errors.
- Evaluated both ApiCompat projects with `DotNetBuildSourceOnly=true` and confirmed that the new toolset version override is absent.
- Product tests and a complete source-build were not run.

Issues.Title: Fix build failure analysis custom-tool replay IDs
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fix the build-failure-analysis agent's terminal HTTP 400 when replaying an `apply_patch` tool call:

```text
400 Invalid 'input[28].id': 'ctc_call_jte2C7wDoAr59GDuD0wTx9hY'.
Expected an ID that begins with 'fc'.
```

The pinned AWF v0.28.23 proxy translates `custom_tool_call` into `function_call` but retains the incompatible `ctc_` item ID. Retrying the same conversation cannot repair that history. The upstream fix, [github/gh-aw-firewall#8944](https://github.com/github/gh-aw-firewall/pull/8944), normalizes the item ID while preserving `call_id`.

- Pin AWF v0.28.66 and all four matching infrastructure images by digest in both automatic and slash-command workflows.
- Regenerate both locks with gh-aw v0.89.22 and its SHA-pinned setup action. This minimal compiler patch is necessary because v0.89.21 drops the explicit image manifest from threat detection; [github/gh-aw#63014](https://github.com/github/gh-aw/pull/63014) fixes that propagation.
- Update the shared regeneration guidance, including the requirement to keep `sandbox` configuration in each top-level caller.

The compiler patch also updates its generated MCP gateway dependency from v0.4.25 to v0.4.26. Workflow triggers, permissions, model selection, network policy, safe-output targets, and telemetry correlation are unchanged.

## Evidence

Original failure: https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/38951682250/job/117146983226#step:31:440

All 11 agent-job failures in the sampled failed runs have the same terminal malformed-tool-ID error with AWF v0.28.23, across three Copilot CLI versions:

| Run | Copilot CLI | Rejected input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [38984274258](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/38984274258/job/117253779876) | 1.0.98 | `input[151].id` |
| [38951682250](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/38951682250/job/117146983226) | 1.0.98 | `input[28].id` |
| [38640693514](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/38640693514/job/116118097121) | 1.0.96 | `input[112].id` |
| [38621937983](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/38621937983/job/116054987783) | 1.0.96 | `input[251].id` |
| [38489606115](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/38489606115/job/115613679537) | 1.0.96 | `input[184].id` |
| [38488885053](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/38488885053/job/115610975227) | 1.0.96 | `input[204].id` |
| [38485690863](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/38485690863/job/115600587878) | 1.0.96 | `input[23].id` |
| [38484607030](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/38484607030/job/115596812101) | 1.0.96 | `input[228].id` |
| [38476588758](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/38476588758/job/115570421728) | 1.0.96 | `input[233].id` |
| [38317867263](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/38317867263/job/115040660972) | 1.0.95 | `input[157].id` |
| [38282380332](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/38282380332/job/114925250786) | 1.0.95 | `input[126].id` |

The other three sampled failures stopped before agent startup in the daily-credit lookup and are separate from this fix.

## Validation

- Both workflows compile successfully with gh-aw v0.89.22 using `--strict --approve --validate --validate-images`; repeated generation produces identical locks.
- Replayed all 11 recorded failing IDs inside the exact digest-pinned v0.28.66 API proxy image, with networking disabled. Every call is converted to `function_call` with an `fc_` item ID, unchanged `call_id`, and preserved patch arguments.
- Compared generated YAML and AWF runtime configuration against the base commit: both agent and detection jobs use the explicit immutable image manifest; policy, permissions, model configuration, triggers, and telemetry are preserved. All generated external action references remain SHA-pinned.
- Pinned actionlint v1.7.12 reports exactly the same diagnostics on the baseline and updated locks (11 automatic, 10 command): existing PAT-pool ShellCheck/`github.aw` findings and unsupported `copilot-requests`/`concurrency.queue` fields. No new lint findings.
- `git diff --check` passes. No live production workflow has been rerun.

Issues.Title: Stabilize SDK layout metadata and JSON finalization
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Bottom layer (PR 1 of 2) of the SDK layout incrementality work, targeting `main`.

- Preserve timestamps for unchanged bundled-version metadata and RID-chain output; track RID/package/implementation changes and successful chain-generation completion separately.
- Finalize deps/runtimeconfig JSON directly from immutable inputs and publish only changed final bytes.
- Keep F# synthetic publish inputs in intermediate storage while shipping only the compiler payload and finalized fsc/fsi configuration.
- Include focused task/layout coverage, required Helix payload declarations, and minimal layout guidance.

The intended follow-up PR covers apphost generation/signing incrementality and copy-target behavior. Those implementations, their tests, and entitlement payload declarations are deliberately excluded here. Native stack registration will wait until the upper PR exists.

## Validation

- Full isolated Debug SDK/redist build succeeded.
- Focused `sdk-tasks.Tests` metadata/RID and JSON/runtimeconfig task/layout suites: **21 passed**, **0 failed**, **0 skipped** (6.46 seconds).
- Preserved the reduced test selection from the pinned source snapshot; no trimmed tests were restored.
- Verified slice boundaries, documentation links, and `git diff --check`.

Slice boundary: `_PublishRoslynFiles` is extracted so JSON coverage can run independently; `PublishRoslyn` retains its original apphost/signing implementation.

Issues.Body:
# [release/11.0.1xx] Fix dotnet watch shutdown with connected browser tools

Cancel browser-tools forwarding when the application stops.

## Description

Backports #56643 to `release/11.0.1xx`. Ensures applications started with `dotnet watch` shut down promptly and cleanly when browser tools are connected.

Fixes #56584

## Customer Impact

Stopping ASP.NET Core applications with connected browser tools can take five seconds and report `Exited with error code -1`. Reported with the .NET 11 SDK, including applications targeting .NET 8, 9, and 10.

## Regression?

- [x] Yes
- [ ] No

Reported as a regression in .NET 11 RC2 and RTM daily builds.

## Risk

- [ ] High
- [ ] Medium
- [x] Low

Limited to browser-tools WebSocket shutdown cancellation. HTTP forwarding and provider handshakes are unchanged; tests cover connected browsers, clean shutdown logging, and reconnection after restarts.

## Verification

- [ ] Manual (required)
- [x] Automated

## Packaging changes reviewed?

- [ ] Yes
- [ ] No
- [x] N/A

No packaging changes.

----

- [ ] Make necessary changes in eng/PatchConfig.props

N/A for `release/11.0.1xx`.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-96960 | .NET and Visual Studio Denial of Service Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml; System.Private.Xml. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Signed XML fixes add input-depth and operation-count limits, prohibit DTD processing by default, validate entity references, bound encrypted-data candidate processing, and cap attributes and namespaces used by C14N transforms. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135711 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-405 (Asymmetric Resource Consumption (Amplification)) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.12 | 10.0.13 [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.4 | 8.0.5 [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.20 | 9.0.21 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.32 Runtime or .NET 8.0.426 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.21 Runtime or .NET 9.0.319 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.13 Runtime or .NET 10.0.402 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. * If you're using .NET 11.0, you should download and install .NET 11.0.0-rc.2 Runtime or .NET 11.0.100-rc.2 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/11.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime; System.Private.CoreLib. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Unix named-mutex and shared-memory paths can be manipulated through insecure global directories, symlink races, and unsafe permission changes, allowing local attackers to truncate or overwrite files, widen directory permissions, or elevate privileges. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135707 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-59 (Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The elevated SDK workload installer can follow a junction or symlink under `%ProgramData%\dotnet`, enabling local privilege escalation. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56612 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.3 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-59 (Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- .NET SDK | >= 11.0.100-preview.1, <= 11.0.100-rc.1 | 11.0.100-rc.2 .NET SDK | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.401 | 10.0.402 .NET SDK | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.112 | 10.0.113 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.
